properties.note: The Tennessee River takes its name from the Cherokee town of Tanasi. It was the main water route for Cherokee trade, travel, and raids for centuries.
Cherokee towns along the Little Tennessee formed the Overhill division: Chota, Tanasi, Tuskegee, Tomotley, and Citico. Most are now submerged under Tellico Lake.
A major river of the Cherokee homeland, running from the southern Appalachians into the Tennessee River.
One of the oldest rivers in the world. Ran through Middle and Out Town country in present-day North Carolina.
Formed by the junction of the Etowah and Oostanaula rivers at Rome, Georgia. A major artery of the Lower Towns and Creek country to the south.
Home to the Etowah Mounds, a major Mississippian-era ceremonial site later associated with Cherokee territory.
Site of the 1814 Battle of Horseshoe Bend, where Cherokee warriors fought alongside Jackson against the Red Stick Creeks.
Flows through the ancestral lands of the Oconaluftee Cherokee, whose descendants form the core of the Eastern Band today.
